name: Hudbay Minerals Inc.
moat_justification: Copper/gold miner and pure commodity price taker: no pricing power, no switching costs, reserves deplete and must be replaced with heavy capex. Only moat-like traits are cost-curve position (gold by-product credits drove Q2 2026 consolidated cash cost to -$0.40/lb Cu), long-life diversified mines in Canada, Peru and the US, and a staged growth pipeline. Measured returns confirm the weak moat: roic_proxy was 0.6% in FY2021, 6.2% in FY2022, 7.2% in FY2023 and 9.8% in FY2024 — below the cost of capital through most of the cycle — reaching 15.4% only in FY2025 at strong metal prices, and gross margin swung from 8.7% (FY2021) to 33.6% (FY2025) with metal prices, not with any pricing power (fundamentals.json).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 14.8%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-27, accession via EDGAR filing 000106299326001648, fundamentals.json latest_filings), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares, no par value', trading symbol HBM, The New York Stock Exchange; the cover reports 395,521,903 common shares outstanding as at December 31, 2025, matching the engine's DEI count of 395,521,903) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
one_liner: Copper price-taker with a low-cost by-product-credit position, moat 3/10 — Tier D: weighted IRR 5.59% and weighted IV@15% $5.66 vs the $23.62 price on the normalized $0.6059/share base, with every scenario including super bull (8.58%) in Tier D; it clears 15% only at or below $5.66, and the filed base does not yet reflect the ~12% share issuance for Arizona Sonoran in June 2026.
moat_for: Low cost-curve position: gold by-product credits drove Q2 2026 consolidated cash cost to -$0.40/lb Cu and sustaining cash cost to $1.39/lb (company Q2 2026 release, cited search result)

Long-life diversified operating base: Constancia (Peru), Snow Lake/Manitoba and Copper Mountain (BC), with reserve lives extended into the 2040s in the company's three-year outlook (cited search result)

Staged copper growth pipeline in tier-1 jurisdictions: Copper World, Cactus (Arizona Sonoran, closed June 2026) and Mason, targeting ~24% higher consolidated copper production by 2027-28 (company guidance, cited search results)
moat_against: Pure commodity price taker — copper and gold prices are set by the market; no pricing power or switching costs
Reserves deplete: production must be replaced via heavy sustaining/growth capex, permitting and M&A (FY2025 capex $466,700,000 vs OCF $707,300,000)
Returns below the cost of capital through most of the cycle: roic_proxy 0.6%-9.8% in FY2021-24, only 15.4% in FY2025 at strong prices (fundamentals.json)

Jurisdiction and execution risk: Peru operations, permitting timelines, and large pre-production projects (Copper World FID expected later in 2026, first production targeted H2 2029, cited search result)

Serial share issuance for M&A: diluted count 261,462,323 in FY2021 to 396,648,796 in FY2025, plus the all-share Arizona Sonoran deal closed June 24, 2026 (financials_history.csv; cited search results)
